answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut and 14-day deadline create urgency, but the 94% line utilization eliminates switching risk tolerance. Memory_c4 demonstrates that benchmarking-driven renegotiation recovered margin without service disruption; memory_c2 shows that cost cuts are achievable through vendor changes—but only if execution is clean. The verification will confirm whether negotiation leverage exists at renewal (c4 precedent) and whether the incumbent's onboarding speed/accuracy (c6 multi-year precedent) justifies renewal over a costlier switch. Negotiating terms preserves the incumbent relationship while targeting the 18% cut through price/terms realignment—lower risk than switching with no buffer. If negotiation fails to meet the 18% target, defer_decision becomes the fallback, using month-to-month continuity (c5 precedent) to buy time for a planned switch in the next cycle when line utilization is healthier.
